project.name: glaze
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected here is the bundled glaze checkout at `17d81a64b4f8c6824ff119f82cce8419b35791f4`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `cf787ad6517ac86f9a3c9719c546757b14fc7a9b`. Its line map matches the saved ASan stack (`include/glaze/json/read.hpp:543`, `process_arithmetic_boolean_string_or_array:2613`, `read_json:3266`, `fuzzing/json_generic.cpp:29`), and the staged `patch.diff` fixes that exact null-terminated boolean parser by replacing the blind 5-byte read with a 4-byte read plus an explicit end check before consuming the trailing `'e'` of `false`.

classification.classification_note: The saved report already identifies a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` at `include/glaze/json/read.hpp:543`. The vulnerable-source trace grounds that overread as the null-terminated `bool` fast path blindly copying five bytes when only four logical input bytes remain.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 425413855 (glaze): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 5 found by fuzz target json_generic [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/425413855
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json.issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged patch.diff / exact staged vulnerable source / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 3-byte file `66 20 20` (`"f  "`). In the crashing const-buffer path at `fuzzing/json_generic.cpp:29`, the fuzz target copies those three bytes into a `std::vector<char>` and appends one `\0`, so Glaze receives a logical 4-byte span `66 20 20 00`; because that call passes `const auto& input`, `glz::read()` does not add SWAR padding. `glz::json_t`'s variant parser sees the leading `'f'` and dispatches into `glz::from<JSON, bool>::op`. Inside that function, the only non-padded length guard is `size_t(end - it) < 4`; on this witness `end - it == 4`, so the guard passes even though the token is truncated. Because `read_json()` uses the default `opts{}` with `null_terminated = true`, the bool fast path then assumes it may read one extra byte without checking and executes `std::memcpy(&c, it, 5)` while only four bytes from `it` to `end` are addressable. The saved ASan trace therefore reports the first invalid byte at `it + 4` and a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` at `include/glaze/json/read.hpp:543:16`. The staged patch removes this blind 5-byte read by loading four bytes first and explicitly bailing out on `it == end` before checking the trailing `'e'` of `false`.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled parsing extent used by the later boolean fast path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has sha256 `b1d78bb3b6188fe285f7acfac5a1caf026aa824560ad55041c7e8bab6d6ce208` and exact bytes `66 20 20`. In the crashing `json_generic.cpp:29` call, the harness appends one `\0` at line 23 and passes a const vector, so `use_padded` is false and this statement materializes `it` at the first `0x66` byte and `end = it + 4` over the logical span `66 20 20 00`.
source.note: Source. This is the first project statement that turns the witness bytes into the `it..end` state consumed by the JSON parser; the missing bound check later depends on the fact that only four bytes are in-range from `it` to `end`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The null-terminated boolean fast path copies five bytes from a four-byte logical input span.
sink.note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` both report `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` at `include/glaze/json/read.hpp:543:16` in the bool parser.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The null-terminated boolean fast path performs a fixed 5-byte read without proving that five bytes remain between `it` and `end`.
root_cause.note: On the witnessed path, the preceding guard only established `end - it >= 4`, and the `Opts.null_terminated` branch omitted any `end - it >= 5` check before this memcpy. The staged patch fixes that exact obligation by reading four bytes first and explicitly rejecting `false` when `it == end` before probing the fifth byte.

parser_admitted.description: The saved crashing path does not require the JSON text to be accepted as valid. It only requires the generic `json_t` dispatch to take the bool arm on leading `'f'` and this 4-byte guard to pass with `end - it == 4`, which is exactly what the staged witness and stack establish before the unsafe memcpy executes.

tainted_value_origin.description: This materializes the exact remaining-byte count later checked as `size_t(end - it)` and then overrun by the 5-byte boolean memcpy.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the exact staged 3-byte witness `66 20 20`, the crashing const-buffer `read_json()` call appends one terminator and leaves `end - it == 4` over `66 20 20 00`, with no extra parser padding.

fine_trace.note: Source. In the crashing `json_generic.cpp:29` call, `input` is const, so `use_padded` is false and the parser uses the vector's current size instead of appending `padding_bytes`. After the harness copies the 3-byte witness and appends one `\0`, this statement yields exactly four logical bytes `66 20 20 00` from `it` to `end`.

The generic `json_t` variant parser consumes the first attacker byte from step 1. Because `*it == 'f'` on the staged witness, it takes the bool arm and routes control into the boolean parser instead of the string, number, array, or object paths.

Present guard. The bool parser derives the remaining logical extent from step 1 and only rejects inputs with fewer than four bytes left. On the staged `66 20 20 00` span, `size_t(end - it) == 4`, so this guard falls through even though the token is still too short for the later 5-byte `false` probe.

fine_trace.code:
if constexpr (Opts.null_terminated) {
   // Note that because our buffer must be null terminated, we can read one more index without checking:
fine_trace.note: Missing guard. `read_json()` uses the default `opts{}` whose `null_terminated` field is true, so the bool parser selects this fast path after step 3. That branch assumes the terminator justifies one unchecked extra byte and never proves `end - it >= 5` before probing a possible `false` token.

Root cause and sink. This copies five bytes from the cursor materialized in step 1 even though only four logical bytes are addressable from `it` to `end`. On the exact witness, ASan marks the first invalid byte at `it + 4` and reports the saved `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` at this line. The staged patch replaces this blind read with a 4-byte load plus an explicit end check before reading the final `'e'` of `false`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged `patch.diff` deletes the null-terminated branch's blind `std::memcpy(&c, it, 5);`, reads only four bytes first, and explicitly returns `unexpected_end` when `it == end` before checking the fifth `e` of `false`. That enforces the missing `end - it >= 5` obligation on the exact witnessed path.

poc.trigger: The staged 3-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `b1d78bb3b6188fe285f7acfac5a1caf026aa824560ad55041c7e8bab6d6ce208`) reproduces Stage 01's saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 5` in `glz::from<10u, bool>::op` when `json_generic` executes its const-buffer `read_json()` block.

format.name: 3-byte truncated JSON boolean token
format.contract: Use the exact 3-byte witness `66 20 20` (`"f  "`). Under the staged `json_generic` fuzz target, those three bytes must still be copied into the const-buffer `read_json()` call at line 29 and extended only with the single terminator from line 23, so Glaze sees exactly four logical bytes `66 20 20 00` with no added padding. The first byte must remain `0x66` so `json_t` dispatch takes the bool arm, and the file must remain exactly three bytes long so the bool parser passes its 4-byte guard yet still lacks a fifth in-range byte before `std::memcpy(&c, it, 5)`. The staged evidence does not establish a broader trigger class than this exact witness and this const-buffer call path.
